tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

schema.name: Glob
schema.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

schema.name: Grep
schema.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

content.content:
1	# Rig card — VTI
2	
3	*Rig-level machine facts for the Sharpe Lab VTI (variable-temperature
4	insert) cryostat. Canonical copy: `hera/rig-cards/VTI.md` in the
5	`measurement-env` repo; deployed as `rig_card.md` next to
6	`device_card.md` in the measurement directory. Errors or gaps found
7	in-session go to `session_notes.md`, not this file — agents are
8	read-only on the repo.*
9	
10	## Identity
11	- **Rig**: VTI — wet variable-temperature insert (closed-loop He
12	  recirculation), out-of-plane magnet
13	- **Rig owner**: Bingcheng (VTI czar) — adjudicates envelope and
14	  operating-edge questions
15	- **Control PC**: `dgg-vti` (Windows 11); measurement dirs under
16	  `~/VTI_local_data/<user>/<session>/`
17	- **Base temperature**: ≈ 1.2–1.3 K; electron temperature ≈ 8 K
18	- **Status**: in service
19	
20	## Magnet
21	
22	- **Supply / driver**: CAEN ELS FAST-PS 1K5, `drivers.FastBi1K5`
23	  (raw TCP `192.168.0.10:10001`). Out-of-plane field, Tesla, via the
24	  `field` qcodes Parameter.
25	- **Coil constant**: `T_per_A = 1/7.3` ≈ 0.137 T/A.
26	- **Ramp rate**: fixed 1 A/min ≈ **0.137 T/min**, hard-coded in the
27	  driver and sent with every setpoint. An 8 T traverse is a ~58 min
28	  floor.
29	- **Set semantics**: `magnet.field(target)` **blocks** until the field
30	  is reached (polls the ramping flag, then a `settle_s` dwell — default
31	  3 s, tunable). A cell that ramps is busy the whole ramp.
32	- **Interrupt ≠ stop**: interrupting the notebook cell does **not**
33	  stop the supply — it keeps ramping to the last setpoint. There is no
34	  abort/pause/ramp-to-zero method; recovery is calling `field()` again
35	  with a new target. Aborting a ramp is the operator acting on the
36	  instrument, never a kernel interrupt.
37	- **Magnet limit**: **14.0 T** (Zack ruling 2026-06-12), enforced by
38	  the driver (`max_field_T = 14.0`; ramping above it raises). The
39	  session cap (device card / SAFETIES, machine-enforced via
40	  `magnet.field.vals`) is what measurements obey.
41	- **High field + elevated T interact through the probe's coupling to
42	  the bath**; not expected to bite below ~100 K (heuristic — Aaron,
43	  2026-08-02, bath-vs-probe-T response unmeasured).
44	- **Read-truth**: `field()`'s get returns the **measured** output

  stop the supply — it keeps ramping to the last setpoint. There is no
  abort/pause/ramp-to-zero method; recovery is calling `field()` again
  with a new target. Aborting a ramp is the operator acting on the
  instrument, never a kernel interrupt.

  session cap (device card / SAFETIES, machine-enforced via

```python
# slot: gate-validators — operating limits from the device card's gate-
# operating-limits table; commit EXACTLY the card numbers. Each value
# `# <-- validate`. Instrument-level fences go on the RAW instruments
# (k_2400_tg / k_2400_bg / dc205); direct calls bypass the role-alias wrapper.
TG_MIN, TG_MAX = -0.3, +1.0    # top gate (k_2400_tg), V     # <-- validate
BG_MIN, BG_MAX = -1.3, +2.0    # back gate (k_2400_bg), V    # <-- validate
SI_MIN, SI_MAX = -25.0, +25.0  # Si gate (dc205), V          # <-- validate
k_2400_tg.volt.vals = validators.Numbers(TG_MIN, TG_MAX)
k_2400_bg.volt.vals = validators.Numbers(BG_MIN, BG_MAX)
dc205.smart_voltage.vals = validators.Numbers(SI_MIN, SI_MAX)  # k_si sets go through this
dc205.voltage.vals = validators.Numbers(SI_MIN, SI_MAX)  # instrument-level: ramp_voltage sets via dc205.voltage, so this fences ramps too

# Limit lists for sanitize_tg_bg()
tg_lims, bg_lims = [TG_MIN, TG_MAX], [BG_MIN, BG_MAX]

# Session field cap — machine-enforced: magnet.field is a qcodes Parameter,
# so this validator rejects any magnet.field(target) with |B| > B_SESSION_CAP
# before any hardware traffic (and the non-blocking start_field_ramp re-checks
# it too). (Driver max_field_T = 14.0 remains as backstop.)

import numpy as np

from pathlib import Path

    summarize_run,
    fan_grids,

    GateCalibration,
    luttinger_frequency,

%matplotlib inline


def _resolve_data_dir():
    """Locate this run's ./data dir from the notebook's own location.

    The ana kernel's cwd is not guaranteed to be the measurement dir, so a
    bare './data' breaks loaders with FileNotFoundError. IPython sets
    globals()['_dh'] to a list whose first entry is the notebook's startup
    cwd (the dir holding the notebook); this survives jupyter-collaboration/
    RTC and any later %cd, so we prefer it. We fall back to Path.cwd() and
    search a few levels up so loading still works if the kernel started inside
    ./data/<id>/. The walk stops before the filesystem root so an unrelated
    top-level 'data' dir can never be matched.
    """
    candidates = []
    dh = globals().get("_dh")
    if dh:
        candidates.append(Path(dh[0]))
    candidates.append(Path.cwd())
    for base in candidates:
        base = Path(base).resolve()
        for d in [base, *base.parents]:
            if d == d.parent:  # filesystem root
                break
            cand = d / "data"
            if cand.is_dir():
                return str(cand)
    return str((Path(candidates[0]) / "data").resolve())


file_path = _resolve_data_dir()


# Open a run by id: run(119) -> Run. Run.col(name) for a column;
# summarize_run(run(119)) for a recipe / range / completeness / T glance.
def run(i):
    return open_run(Path(file_path) / str(i))

## (n, D) — capacitance-based convention

`GateCalibration` carries the gate->(n, D) lever arm: `cal.n_D(V_tg, V_bg)`
returns `n` in SI (m^-2; ×1e-16 for 10^12 cm^-2) and `D` in V/m. Build it from
the gate-stack thicknesses with `from_thicknesses` (κ_hBN/κ_SiO2 default).

form. Set `n_offset` / `D_offset` from `cnp-and-dline-calibration` once the CNP

            if d == d.parent:  # filesystem root
                break
            cand = d / "data"
            if cand.is_dir():
                return str(cand)
    return str((Path(candidates[0]) / "data").resolve())


file_path = _resolve_data_dir()

# summarize_run(run(119)) for a recipe / range / completeness / T glance.
def run(i):
    return open_run(Path(file_path) / str(i))

## (n, D) — capacitance-based convention

`GateCalibration` carries the gate->(n, D) lever arm: `cal.n_D(V_tg, V_bg)`
returns `n` in SI (m^-2; ×1e-16 for 10^12 cm^-2) and `D` in V/m. Build it from
the gate-stack thicknesses with `from_thicknesses` (κ_hBN/κ_SiO2 default).
This is the capacitance convention, **not** the toploader's `dtg/dbg` constant
form. Set `n_offset` / `D_offset` from `cnp-and-dline-calibration` once the CNP
/ D-line is live.

172

180	### `GateCalibration` (frozen dataclass)
181	`GateCalibration(c_tg, c_bg, n_offset=0.0, D_offset=0.0)` — areal capacitances
182	(F/m²), `n_offset` (m⁻²), `D_offset` (V/m). Construct once per session, then:
183	
184	```
185	n = (c_tg·V_tg + c_bg·V_bg) / e   + n_offset      [m⁻²]
186	D = (c_tg·V_tg − c_bg·V_bg) / (2·ε₀) + D_offset   [V/m]
187	```
188	
189	- `density(V_tg, V_bg)` → n `(m⁻²)`.
190	- `displacement_field(V_tg, V_bg)` → D `(V/m)`.
191	- `n_D(V_tg, V_bg)` → `(n, D)`.
192	- `from_thicknesses(t_tg, t_bg, t_bgSiO2=0.0, *, n_offset=0.0, D_offset=0.0, kappa_hBN=3.0, kappa_SiO2=3.9)` — build from gate-stack geometry (metres) instead of areal capacitances; `t_bgSiO2=0` for a metal/graphite back gate.
193	
194	All accept scalars or arrays. Physical constants come from `scipy.constants`.
195	
196	### `luttinger_frequency(n)` → `np.ndarray`
197	Full-density Onsager (SdH) frequency `F = |n|·h / (4·e)`, in Tesla, for a
198	single Fermi surface carrying the full density. **`n` is in SI m⁻²** — feed
199	`GateCalibration.density` output directly. The 4 is the spin×valley Landau
200	degeneracy; returns the `|n|` form (positive for either carrier sign).

`win_invB` (actual filter geometry), `harmonic_of` (freq of the stronger tone
this sits at ~k× of, else `None`), curves `b_centers` / `snr` / `amp`, and
`delta_f(b_max)` — the per-tone FFT resolution `1/(1/onset_b − 1/b_max)`.

---

## Gate calibration

> **Units — SI.** `GateCalibration` and `luttinger_frequency` work entirely in
> SI: density **n in m⁻²**, displacement field **D in V/m**, frequency in
> Tesla. (For the conventional ×10¹² cm⁻² display unit, scale n by `1e-16`.)
> The separate `sharpelab_nb.gates` conversion helpers (`calc_nD`,
> `calc_gate_voltages`, …) use **n in 10¹² cm⁻²** — do not feed an SI density
> from here into those, or vice versa.

### `GateCalibration` (frozen dataclass)
`GateCalibration(c_tg, c_bg, n_offset=0.0, D_offset=0.0)` — areal capacitances
(F/m²), `n_offset` (m⁻²), `D_offset` (V/m). Construct once per session, then:

```
n = (c_tg·V_tg + c_bg·V_bg) / e   + n_offset      [m⁻²]
D = (c_tg·V_tg − c_bg·V_bg) / (2·ε₀) + D_offset   [V/m]
```

- `density(V_tg, V_bg)` → n `(m⁻²)`.
- `displacement_field(V_tg, V_bg)` → D `(V/m)`.
- `n_D(V_tg, V_bg)` → `(n, D)`.
- `from_thicknesses(t_tg, t_bg, t_bgSiO2=0.0, *, n_offset=0.0, D_offset=0.0, kappa_hBN=3.0, kappa_SiO2=3.9)` — build from gate-stack geometry (metres) instead of areal capacitances; `t_bgSiO2=0` for a metal/graphite back gate.

All accept scalars or arrays. Physical constants come from `scipy.constants`.

### `luttinger_frequency(n)` → `np.ndarray`
Full-density Onsager (SdH) frequency `F = |n|·h / (4·e)`, in Tesla, for a
single Fermi surface carrying the full density. **`n` is in SI m⁻²** — feed
`GateCalibration.density` output directly. The 4 is the spin×valley Landau
degeneracy; returns the `|n|` form (positive for either carrier sign).

input.content:
"""SdH spot checks, runs 6 (electron, n=+3.2e12, 0->10 T) and 7 (hole, n=-1.2e12, 10->0.3 T):
raw R(B), background-subtracted oscillatory part, 1/B FFT, per-tone onset via hera.analysis.sdh_onset."""
import sys, json, numpy as np, matplotlib, warnings
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from hera.analysis import open_run, resolve_channels, current_channel, sdh_fft, sdh_onset, luttinger_frequency
from scipy.constants import e, h

def load(rid):
    r = open_run(f"data/{rid}")
    chs = resolve_channels(r.meta)
    cur = current_channel(chs)
    I = r.col(cur.col) / cur.gain
    v = [c for c in chs if c.cid == "sr1"][0]
    R = (r.col(v.col) / v.gain) / I
    B = r.col("magnet_field")
    o = np.argsort(B)
    return r, B[o], R[o], I[o], r.col("T_sample")[o], chs

out = {}
fig, axs = plt.subplots(3, 2, figsize=(14, 12))
for j, (rid, n12) in enumerate([(6, 3.2), (7, -1.2)]):
    r, B, R, I, T, chs = load(rid)
    mc = r.meta["measurement_config"]
    sens = None
    try:
        sens = r.meta["instruments"]["sr1"]["parameters"]["sensitivity"]["value"]
    except Exception:
        pass
    Ib = np.median(I)
    print(f"\n===== run {rid}: n = {n12:+.1f}e12, {len(B)} pts, B {B.min():.2f}-{B.max():.2f} T, T_sample {T.mean():.3f} +/- {T.std():.3f} K, I_bias med {Ib*1e9:.3f} nA, sr1 sens {sens}")
    print(f"  R(B<0.1) = {np.median(R[B<0.15]):.1f} Ohm; R range {R.min():.1f} .. {R.max():.1f} Ohm; R at 10T {R[-1]:.1f}")
    FL = luttinger_frequency(abs(n12) * 1e16)
    print(f"  Luttinger full-density frequency F_L = {FL:.2f} T (single 4-fold FS); n from F: F * 4e/h = {FL*4*e/h*1e-16:.2f}e12")
    ax = axs[0, j]; ax.plot(B, R, lw=0.8); ax.set_xlabel("B (T)"); ax.set_ylabel("Rxx (Ohm)"); ax.set_title(f"run {rid}: n={n12:+.1f}e12, D=0, raw Rxx(B)")
    # local minima/maxima positions >1.5 T (oscillation extrema)
    from scipy.signal import find_peaks
    from scipy.ndimage import gaussian_filter1d
    sel = B > 1.0
    Rs = gaussian_filter1d(R[sel], 1.5)
    pk, _ = find_peaks(Rs, prominence=3); mn, _ = find_peaks(-Rs, prominence=3)
    print(f"  maxima (B>1T): {np.round(B[sel][pk], 2).tolist()}")
    print(f"  minima (B>1T): {np.round(B[sel][mn], 2).tolist()}")
    # 1/B of minima and their spacing
    if len(mn) > 2:
        ib = 1 / B[sel][mn]; d = -np.diff(ib)
        print(f"  1/B minima spacings (1/T): {np.round(d, 4).tolist()} -> F ~ {np.round(1/d, 1).tolist()} T")
    # FFT in 1/B over a couple of windows
    for (blo, bhi) in [(1.5, 10.0), (2.0, 6.0), (4.0, 10.0)]:
        m = (B >= blo) & (B <= bhi)
        try:
            f, spec = sdh_fft(R[m][:, None], B[m], nfft=2048, bg_degree=5, log=False)
            sp = spec[0]; fm = f > 2
            top = np.argsort(sp[fm])[::-1][:6]
            fp_, _ = find_peaks(sp[fm], prominence=0.15 * sp[fm].max())
            print(f"  FFT [{blo},{bhi}] T: peaks at F = {np.round(f[fm][fp_], 1).tolist()} T (amp rel {np.round(sp[fm][fp_]/sp[fm].max(), 2).tolist()})")
            if (blo, bhi) == (1.5, 10.0):
                ax2 = axs[2, j]; ax2.plot(f, sp, lw=0.8); ax2.set_xlim(0, 60); ax2.set_xlabel("F (T)"); ax2.set_ylabel("FFT amp")
                ax2.set_title(f"run {rid} FFT in 1/B, B in [{blo},{bhi}] T, bg deg 5"); ax2.axvline(FL, color="r", ls="--", lw=1, label=f"F_L={FL:.1f} T")
                ax2.axvline(FL/2, color="orange", ls=":", lw=1, label="F_L/2"); ax2.legend(fontsize=8)
        except Exception as ex:
            print(f"  FFT [{blo},{bhi}] failed: {ex}")
    # background-subtracted
    m = B > 1.0
    cf = np.polyfit(B[m], R[m], 5); dR = R[m] - np.polyval(cf, B[m])
    ax1 = axs[1, j]; ax1.plot(1 / B[m], dR, lw=0.8); ax1.set_xlabel("1/B (1/T)"); ax1.set_ylabel("dRxx (Ohm)"); ax1.set_title(f"run {rid}: Rxx minus deg-5 poly(B), vs 1/B")
    # onset
    rfs = (sens / Ib) if sens else None
    try:
        with warnings.catch_warnings():
            warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
            on = sdh_onset(R, B, b_lo=0.3, r_full_scale=rfs)
        print(on.summary())
        out[rid] = dict(onset_b=float(on.onset_b), onset_freq=float(on.onset_freq),
                        tones=[dict(freq=float(t.freq), contrast=float(t.contrast), onset_b=float(t.onset_b), censored=bool(t.censored), marginal=bool(t.marginal), harmonic_of=(None if t.harmonic_of is None else float(t.harmonic_of))) for t in on.tones])
    except Exception as ex:
        print(f"  sdh_onset failed: {ex}")
fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig("hera_scratch/spot_runs6_7.png", dpi=110)
json.dump(out, open("hera_scratch/spot_onsets.json", "w"), indent=1)
print("\nsaved hera_scratch/spot_runs6_7.png")

    from scipy.ndimage import gaussian_filter1d
    sel = B > 1.0
    Rs = gaussian_filter1d(R[sel], 1.5)
    pk, _ = find_peaks(Rs, prominence=3); mn, _ = find_peaks(-Rs, prominence=3)
    print(f"  maxima (B>1T): {np.round(B[sel][pk], 2).tolist()}")
    print(f"  minima (B>1T): {np.round(B[sel][mn], 2).tolist()}")
    # 1/B of minima and their spacing
    if len(mn) > 2:
        ib = 1 / B[sel][mn]; d = -np.diff(ib)
        print(f"  1/B minima spacings (1/T): {np.round(d, 4).tolist()} -> F ~ {np.round(1/d, 1).tolist()} T")
    # FFT in 1/B over a couple of windows
    for (blo, bhi) in [(1.5, 10.0), (2.0, 6.0), (4.0, 10.0)]:
        m = (B >= blo) & (B <= bhi)
        try:
            f, spec = sdh_fft(R[m][:, None], B[m], nfft=2048, bg_degree=5, log=False)
            sp = spec[0]; fm = f > 2
            top = np.argsort(sp[fm])[::-1][:6]
            fp_, _ = find_peaks(sp[fm], prominence=0.15 * sp[fm].max())
            print(f"  FFT [{blo},{bhi}] T: peaks at F = {np.round(f[fm][fp_], 1).tolist()} T (amp rel {np.round(sp[fm][fp_]/sp[fm].max(), 2).tolist()})")
            if (blo, bhi) == (1.5, 10.0):
                ax2 = axs[2, j]; ax2.plot(f, sp, lw=0.8); ax2.set_xlim(0, 60); ax2.set_xlabel("F (T)"); ax2.set_ylabel("FFT amp")
                ax2.set_title(f"run {rid} FFT in 1/B, B in [{blo},{bhi}] T, bg deg 5"); ax2.axvline(FL, color="r", ls="--", lw=1, label=f"F_L={FL:.1f} T")
                ax2.axvline(FL/2, color="orange", ls=":", lw=1, label="F_L/2"); ax2.legend(fontsize=8)
        except Exception as ex:
            print(f"  FFT [{blo},{bhi}] failed: {ex}")
    # background-subtracted
    m = B > 1.0
    cf = np.polyfit(B[m], R[m], 5); dR = R[m] - np.polyval(cf, B[m])
    ax1 = axs[1, j]; ax1.plot(1 / B[m], dR, lw=0.8); ax1.set_xlabel("1/B (1/T)"); ax1.set_ylabel("dRxx (Ohm)"); ax1.set_title(f"run {rid}: Rxx minus deg-5 poly(B), vs 1/B")
    # onset
    rfs = (sens / Ib) if sens else None
    try:
        with warnings.catch_warnings():
            warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
            on = sdh_onset(R, B, b_lo=0.3, r_full_scale=rfs)
        print(on.summary())
        out[rid] = dict(onset_b=float(on.onset_b), onset_freq=float(on.onset_freq),
                        tones=[dict(freq=float(t.freq), contrast=float(t.contrast), onset_b=float(t.onset_b), censored=bool(t.censored), marginal=bool(t.marginal), harmonic_of=(None if t.harmonic_of is None else float(t.harmonic_of))) for t in on.tones])
    except Exception as ex:
        print(f"  sdh_onset failed: {ex}")
fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig("hera_scratch/spot_runs6_7.png", dpi=110)
json.dump(out, open("hera_scratch/spot_onsets.json", "w"), indent=1)

# -------------------------------
    # Ramp control
    # -------------------------------
    def _check_target(self, field_target: float) -> None:
        """
        Validate a ramp target before any setpoint is issued: the hard
        magnet limit plus the ``field`` parameter's validator (the session
        cap). The qcodes Parameter layer already runs the validator on
        ``field(target)``; calling it here makes the same cap apply on the
        non-blocking ``start_field_ramp`` path, which bypasses that layer.
        """
        if abs(field_target) > self.max_field_T:
            raise ValueError(f"Target field exceeds maximum field {self.max_field_T} Tesla!")
        self.field.validate(field_target)

    def start_field_ramp(self, field_target: float) -> None:
        """
        Issue a field ramp and return immediately (non-blocking).

        Validates the target, checks supply preconditions, sends the
        setpoint, and stashes (start, target) for ``wait_for_ramp``. Does
        NOT poll the ramp flag or settle. Pair with ``is_ramping`` /
        ``wait_for_ramp`` (or sample lock-ins while ``field()`` is read) to
        measure on the fly.
        """
        self._check_target(field_target)

        status = self._status()
        if status["persistent_switch_on"] == False: # switch heater status check
            raise ValueError(f"Persistent Switch On : {status['persistent_switch_on']}")

        if status["output_enabled"] == False: # magnet controller output check
            raise ValueError(f"Output Enabled       : {status['output_enabled']}")

        current_target    = field_target / self.T_per_A
        slew_A_per_s      = self.slew_T_per_s / self.T_per_A

        self._ramp_start = status["field"]
        self._ramp_target = field_target

        self._write(f"SET:I:{slew_A_per_s}:{current_target}")
        time.sleep(0.1)

    def wait_for_ramp(self, timeout: float | None = None, tol: float | None = None) -> None:
        """
        Block until the in-progress field ramp completes, then settle.

        Phase 1 polls the controller ramp flag (``is_ramping``) until it
        clears. Phase 2 settles: with ``tol=None`` a flat ``settle_s``
        dwell; with ``tol`` set, a dynamic settle that polls the field
        readback until it is within ``tol`` Tesla of the stashed target
        (``tol`` must exceed the ~0.1 mT readback noise or it never
        converges — the timeout then trips).

        ``timeout``: ``None`` auto-bounds from ``|dB|/slew``; a float is a
        hard cap in seconds; ``math.inf`` waits forever. Exceeding it
        raises ``TimeoutError``.
        """
        deadline = self._ramp_deadline(timeout)

        while self.is_ramping():
            self._check_deadline(deadline)
            time.sleep(self.poll_interval_s)

        if tol is None:
            time.sleep(self.settle_s)
            return

        target = self._ramp_target
        while abs(self._get_field() - target) > tol:
            self._check_deadline(deadline)
            time.sleep(self.poll_interval_s)

import numpy as np
from sharpelab_nb.gates import calc_gate_voltages, calc_nD
CAL = dict(c_tg=2.796e-03, c_bg=2.161e-03, n_offset=-0.0894, D_offset=-0.013)
# full D=0 window inside validators
ns = np.linspace(-1.5, 3.6, 5101); Vt, Vb = calc_gate_voltages(ns, 0*ns, **CAL)
ok = (Vt>=-0.3)&(Vt<=1.0)&(Vb>=-1.3)&(Vb<=2.0); print('D=0 realized n window:', ns[ok].min().round(3), ns[ok].max().round(3))
n_vec = np.round(np.arange(-1.25, 3.25001, 0.03), 4); Vtg, Vbg = calc_gate_voltages(n_vec, 0*n_vec, **CAL)
print(len(n_vec), 'pts; Vtg', Vtg.min().round(4), Vtg.max().round(4), '; Vbg', Vbg.min().round(4), Vbg.max().round(4))
print('dVtg/pt', np.diff(Vtg).mean().round(4), 'dVbg/pt', np.diff(Vbg).mean().round(4))
B_rows = np.unique(np.round(np.hstack(([0.0, 0.5, 0.75], 1/np.linspace(1/1.0, 1/5.0, 68), np.arange(5.25, 10.0001, 0.25))), 4))
print(len(B_rows), 'rows; first', B_rows[:6], 'around 5T', B_rows[66:74], 'last', B_rows[-3:])
d = np.diff(1/B_rows[3:71]); print('d(1/B) low leg', d.min().round(4), d.max().round(4), '-> Nyquist F', (0.5/d.max()).round(1), 'T; dB at 1T', np.diff(B_rows[3:6]).round(4), 'at 5T', np.diff(B_rows[68:71]).round(3))
# pricing
npt=len(n_vec); nrow=len(B_rows); per_pt=0.5+0.25; row=npt*per_pt+3+3+6
ramp=10.0/0.137*60
print(f'per row ~{row:.0f} s; rows total {nrow*row/3600:.2f} h; ramp {ramp/60:.0f} min; total {(nrow*row+ramp)/3600:.2f} h; x1.08 -> {(nrow*row+ramp)*1.08/3600:.2f} h; points {npt*nrow}')
# filling-factor lines: n at nu=4 for B=1..10
print('n(nu=4) 1e12 at 1,5,10 T:', [round(4*2.418e10*B/1e12,3) for B in (1,5,10)])
"

# vti-02 stacking-order campaign — plan (reconstructed at handoff, 2026-08-23 ~05:30)

Goal: ABAB vs ABCA vs ABCB for the one measured pair (sr1 = B_1–B_2), evidence-cited, with a
strength word — or a calibrated "cannot tell". No prior data; everything below is this session's.

## Done (steps 0–3)

0. **Gate C** — runs 0–3 (`gate-current-sanity-check`): alive, no leakage, Rxx 60–330 Ω; two series
   CNPs on each gate (regions A and B). PASS.
1. **0 T gatemap** — run 5 (`gatemap`, run 4 railed): ridge A slope → c_bg/c_tg = 0.773 (prior 0.864);
   c_tg anchored at the 9.5 nm prior (absolute n scale still a prior); n_offset −0.089×10¹²;
   D_offset −0.013 V/nm from the R_CNP(D) minimum. Ridge B parallel, 0.43×10¹² electron-doped vs A
   (series mosaic — a confound to carry). CNP gap is D-tunable (240 Ω → 2.4 kΩ at 0.25 V/nm): not a
   stacking read on its own.
2. **Feasibility** — F_L(3.2×10¹²) = 33.1 T; model tones ABAB ≈ 7.5/25.6 T, ABCA 33.1 T.
3. **SdH spot checks** — run 6 (e, n = +3.2, 0→10 T) and run 7 (h, n = −1.2, 10→0.3 T). Read
   (hera_scratch/spot_analysis.py): run 6 has a strong 7.1 T tone with 2×/3×/4× harmonics in 1.5–6 T
   and a lone 33.3 T tone above 4 T (= F_L: total-filling QH sequence); run 7 has 6.6 T (≈F_L/2) and
   12.3 T (= F_L). Two-band low-B regime feeding a single total-density sequence at high B.
   **Not yet landed in the ana notebook — land during the fan.**

## Now — step 4: Landau fan at D = 0 (`landau-fan`) — the stacking measurement

Field slow (magnet at 0 T now → ascend to 10 T, never re-traverse), (V_tg, V_bg) co-swept fast along the
calibrated D = 0 line, n = −1.25…+3.25×10¹² (TG-validator-limited on both ends; hole side stops at
−1.25 — stated coverage trade), step 0.03×10¹² (151 pts). Rows: 0, 0.5, 0.75 T; 68 rows uniform in
1/B from 1 to 5 T (Δ(1/B) = 0.012 T⁻¹ → per-column FFT Nyquist 42 T, covers the 33 T tone); 0.25 T
steps 5→10 T (QH regime read in 2D). 91 rows, ≈ 4.4 h nominal, 4h45m priced.

What it establishes, and the decision rule:
- **Per-band fan lines at low B (1–5 T):** extract tone frequencies vs n (per-column 1/B FFT) and the
  Rxx-minima lines in (n, B). ABCA → one tone at F_L(n) (all lines at integer ν through the CNP; ν = 8+4k
  sequence from the 16-fold zero LL). ABAB → two tones with F_1 + F_2 = F_L and a roughly *constant*
  partition F_1/F_L (both bilayer-like bands parabolic, common band bottom) → straight light-band lines
  through the CNP at non-integer apparent ν (run 6: 7.1/33.1 = 0.215 → apparent Δν ≈ 18.6).
  ABCB → two tones with an *n-dependent* partition (Dirac-like n ∝ E² vs parabolic n ∝ E) → curved
  light-band lines / F_1/F_L rising with n, and possible intercept offset from the intrinsic gap.
- **QH sequence at high B (5–10 T):** which total ν carry gaps near the CNP (±4, ±8, ±12 …) and away
  from it; interleaving of two LL ladders (ABAB/ABCB: level crossings, irregular gap strength vs ν)
  vs a single ladder (ABCA).
- **Absolute n scale:** the slopes of the integer-ν lines (dn/dB = ν e/h) calibrate c_tg — replaces the
  geometry prior; also fixes the CNP (fan apex).
- Checkpoints: row 1 (B = 0 n-trace: CNP at n ≈ 0 ± 0.1, R levels, no leak); ~1.5 T (oscillations along
  n); ~3 T (fan lines present); 5 T (QH minima). Abort on leak trip, a fully railed row, or a featureless
  map at 3 T.

What would change my mind / next after the fan:
- If the fan shows a single ladder (integer ν only, one tone = F_L at all n) → ABCA-leaning; then
  step 5a: check the ν sequence near the CNP at 10 T vs D (the rhombohedral gap opens strongly with D).
- If two ladders → ABAB vs ABCB by the partition-vs-n test above; then step 5b: LK temperature
  dependence of each tone at one or two n (masses: ABAB pair ~0.03/0.06 mₑ; ABCB Dirac band lighter and
  n-dependent) — rides the magnet down from 10 T with `heater.set_both(T, ratio=0.95)` steps, honoring
  the rig card's overshoot/settling facts.
- Region B (series mosaic, +0.43×10¹²): expect a duplicate fan offset in n at ×1.13 frequency; if
  present, report per-region where separable, else fold into the hedge.
- Close-out: `return-to-initial` (field 0, gates 0, heaters off, readback → session_notes).
